title: Games and Films
label: ch:ml-leisure
canDo: I can name a game, say that I play, and name a film.

payoff.summary: From cold: the three leisure words, and what actually decides the letter that slides in before aaNu.
payoff.note: Three atoms. THE EXAM POINT'S OWN NOTE WAS OVERSTATED and is corrected here: it claimed not one leisure word was taught, but vaayikkuka, kaaNuka and pusthakam are all owned, and its lesson count had rotted by well over a hundred files. The real gap was sport, games and shows, and that is what this chapter closes. ozhivusamayam (free time) was REFUSED: samayam is not taught, so the compound would be built out of an unowned part -- the free-time limb of LEX-37 stays open on purpose. THE CHAPTER'S ONE GENERALISING SENTENCE WAS THE DANGER, as in 96 and 97, AND IT WAS WRONG TWICE. ROUND ONE: sinima is the first vowel-final word in the book to join aaNu without ending in -i, and the draft said the ya 'comes anyway' -- which reads as 'a vowel brings ya' and is FALSE of a word the learner already has: pashu (ML-C60-cow) gives pashuvaaNu, with va. ROUND TWO: the replacement, 'the last vowel chooses, and -u takes va', is itself refuted by enthu + aaNu = enthaaNu (ML-C02-entu, sequence 130) and by ithu standing un-glided inside this lesson's own example sentence, because ML-C69-words teaches word-final chandrakkala as a FAINT HALF-U and so makes those words vowel-final by the book's own account. The rule is now stated of FULL vowels only, the half-u gets its own paragraph and its own recall question, and the cow remains the row that goes the other way. FIVE MERGED LESSONS CARRIED THE BROAD YA-RULE, not the three first counted: ML-C97-bhangi in body AND Wrap-up, ML-R97-beauty-recall, ML-C70-um-more, and the neighbours missed on the first pass, ML-C70-um (2390) and ML-C70-o (2410). All five now name the vowel. Also corrected before push: kalikkuka claimed 'eight verbs in this book already end that way' -- a token sweep found SEVEN -ikkuka headwords, and the count would rot on the next verb anyway, so the number was replaced by four named verbs; kali said 'two words now do this' when kuttiyaaNu has done it since sequence 810; kali's Warm-up asked for 'this is beauty', the exact gloss ML-C97-bhangi tells the learner is wrong; and kali's 'first word for something done for its own sake' was a claim nothing could check, narrowed to 'the book's first word for play'.
